name: Functional
how: Decompose by capability or responsibility. Each component owns one coherent set of behaviours.

name: Temporal
how: Decompose by sequence and dependency: what must happen first, second, third. Focus on ordering, prerequisites and the critical path.

name: Risk
how: Decompose by uncertainty and difficulty. Separate known from unknown and easy from hard; group by confidence.

name: Data flow
how: Decompose by information movement: where data originates, where it flows, how it transforms. Boundaries are where data changes shape.

name: User journey
how: Decompose by what the user does, step by step. Each component is a stage in their journey.

name: Failure mode
how: Decompose by what can go wrong. Each component groups the failure modes that share a domain.

name: Interface first
how: Define the contracts between pieces before the pieces. Let the components emerge from what lives on each side of each interface.

name: Ownership
how: Decompose by who will build, own and be paged for each piece. Boundaries follow teams, so the seams are where handoffs and misunderstandings happen.

name: Reversibility
how: Split the decisions into one-way doors (expensive to undo) and two-way doors (cheap to undo). Sequence the one-way doors carefully and move fast through the rest.

name: Constraint
how: Find the one constraint that limits the whole system. Exploit it, make everything else serve it, then raise it, and look for the next one.
source: Goldratt, Theory of Constraints: five focusing steps

name: Is / is not
how: State what, where, when and how much the problem IS, and what it IS NOT though it could be. Any cause must explain that difference.

name: Value chain
how: Start from the user need, list the components that serve it and their dependencies, and mark each as novel, custom, product or commodity. Build only the novel and custom parts.

name: Ecocycle
how: Place every activity in birth, maturity, creative destruction or renewal. Look for the phase where things pile up, and what should be let go.

name: Issue tree
how: Break the question into sub-questions that do not overlap and together cover it, down to questions a single piece of evidence can answer. Each leaf names that evidence.
